williamsonDesign.sourceDivergence: R-prefix rows (source_file=stratmap25-landparcels_48491_lp.zip, the StratMap geometry/parcel roll) and numeric rows (source_file=property.csv, the WCAD appraisal roll) are two independently-ingested sources with unrelated internal numbering. This is why a prefix-strip is structurally wrong, not merely discouraged: there is no arithmetic relationship between an R-account and a numeric account for the same property.
williamsonDesign.crosswalkKey: exact string match on situs_address as the primary derivation (both sources already share a consistent 'STREET, CITY, TX ZIP' format -- a trim() test found zero additional matches over raw equality), restricted to the subset of R-rows where the match is UNIQUE (exactly one numeric counterpart). Ambiguous (many numeric rows share the R-row's situs) and zero-match R-rows are refused, not resolved by any tie-break heuristic.
williamsonDesign.secondDerivation: owner_name, independently populated by each source with different punctuation conventions (e.g. 'BREM, ALEC W & CAITLIN' vs 'BREM  ALEC W & CAITLIN'), compared after regexp_replace(upper(name), '[^A-Z0-9]', '', 'g') normalization.

secondDerivationAgreement.combinedCorroboration: 92.2% of unique situs matches also agree on an independently-sourced field. This is strong evidence the situs join finds the same real-world property rather than colliding by coincidence. The 7.8% non-agreement is not evidence the join is wrong -- property.csv and the StratMap roll are different vintages, so an ownership transfer captured by one and not the other produces a real, honest disagreement. Owner-name agreement is corroborating evidence, not a gate: the crosswalk key is uniqueness of the situs match, not owner agreement.

fanOutMechanism.sampledCase: R022482, situs 'RONALD REAGAN BLVD, LIBERTY HILL, TX 78642' (an arterial address with no house number) fans out to 64 distinct numeric accounts under related commercial entities (SANTA RITA COMMERCIAL LLC, SRFV DEVELOPMENT LLC, SANTA RITA KC LLC, SANTA RITA INVESTMENTS LTD), each a separately platted commercial lot on one large tract sharing an imprecise situs string.
fanOutMechanism.conclusion: ambiguity is a real-world artifact of commercial subdivision, not a data-quality defect a smarter string match would resolve. These 22,701 R-rows must stay unmatched residue; picking any one candidate (e.g. nearest market value) would be exactly the silent mis-join the gap ledger and this card's own instructions prohibit.

prefixStripDisproof.example: R000009 (situs 200 RIO VISTA DR, GEORGETOWN, TX 78626; owner BREM, ALEC W & CAITLIN; market 401306 on the StratMap roll) crosswalks to numeric account 62578 (same situs, same normalized owner, market 394000, improvement 313000, living 2022 on the WCAD roll). A prefix-strip of 'R000009' produces '9', a wholly different and unrelated account. This is concrete proof, not a hypothetical: the prohibition in the gap ledger and this dispatch is correct and load-bearing.

williamsonDesign.residue: 22,701 ambiguous + 2,264 zero-match = 24,965 R-prefix accounts (8.8% of 282,569) are NOT resolved by this crosswalk and must stay unaccounted after R1B's re-ingest runs. R1B must not silently treat these as matched, and must not invent a resolution for the ambiguous set.

williamsonFixturePairs.method: SELECT r_prop_id, n_prop_id, improvement_value, living_area_sqft FROM the unique-situs-match set WHERE owner-name-normalized agreement is exact, ORDER BY r_prop_id, LIMIT 50
williamsonFixturePairs.observation: the sample happens to show near-sequential r_prop_id -> n_prop_id pairing in this early range of the roll (R000009->62578, R000013->62579 ...), which could look like a fixed offset. It is NOT: the offset is not constant across the full 257,604-pair set (spot check elsewhere in the roll breaks any fixed-offset hypothesis), and R022482's 64-way fan-out has no single numeric counterpart at all. Do not generalize an offset from this early-roll sample; the situs+owner join is the mechanism, not an arithmetic pattern.

bastropDesign.adjudicatedContext: gap ledger Mechanism A: 8,712 living>0 and 6,158 $0 CAD accounts have zero overlap against txgio_parcel on the same or zero-padded prop_id. Already ruled: never stamp these onto landing parcels. This card's job is to design where they DO belong.
bastropDesign.finding: the population is NOT one mechanism. It decomposes into at least three, and the two populations named in the gap ledger (living>0 vs $0) sort almost entirely into different mechanisms.

mechanism1MobileHomeOnLand.discovery: legal_description on the sampled orphan accounts reads 'MH ONLY <dims>, SERIAL# ..., LABEL# ... LOCA?TED ON R#####' (note: at least one real row misspells LOCATED as LOCTED -- both spellings must be matched). The R##### is Bastrop's own real-property (land) account number for the parcel the mobile home sits on -- NOT a Williamson-style key scheme; Bastrop's land accounts are themselves plain numeric (e.g. '90026'), and the 'R' here is the legal-description convention for 'real property account', stripped before lookup.
mechanism1MobileHomeOnLand.recommendation: companion representation on the PARENT feature, keyed by the resolved parent prop_id (not the MH account's own prop_id, which has no geometry and never will). This matches the gap ledger's 'if a parent link exists' branch -- one does, and it resolves at 99%+ once the reference is present. The remaining 27.4% of living>0 orphans without a parent-link reference need a second-pass characterization (see leave_behind); they are not necessarily mechanism 2 or 3, just not yet confirmed.

mechanism2NonSpatialPersonalProperty.discovery: of the 6,158 $0-improvement orphans, ZERO carry a parent-land reference -- a structurally different population from the living>0 orphans. A random sample of the largest sub-bucket (5,119 rows with no property_use_code and no land_acres) shows: business personal property ('BUS PERS PROPERTY - LOCATED @ <address>' -- a business location, not a parcel), mineral/royalty fractional-interest accounts (varied legal_description formats, e.g. 'BAZARSKY 30019592-000 .0051975000 O TRIVISTA OPERA/SERBIN...'), utility distribution systems (CenterPoint Energy Entex), and leased equipment / cell-site accounts (AT&T Mobility). None of these correspond to a physical land parcel.
mechanism2NonSpatialPersonalProperty.recommendation: an explicit out-of-fabric register, never a companion link -- these accounts are categorically non-parcel and will never gain geometry. This should be encoded as not-applicable at the module level once this class is formally handled, not left indistinguishable from unaccounted (per ENFORCEMENT.md's absent/zero/unmeasured distinction, applied here to accounts vs parcels: these are not a gap in coverage, they are a different kind of thing).

mechanism3RealAcreageGeometryGap.discovery: 1,037 of the 6,158 $0-improvement orphans carry real land_acres and land_value>0 (D1 agricultural-use code observed in the two spot-checked rows) -- these ARE real land parcels, not personal property, that simply fail to join txgio_parcel.
mechanism3RealAcreageGeometryGap.recommendation: this is a genuine potential geometry-fabric gap (txgio possibly under-covers rural/agricultural parcels in Bastrop), distinct from both mechanisms above. It is NOT solved by this card's crosswalk design and needs its own investigation -- flagged as leave_behind, not closed over.

counts.countingNote: 5416 = 297 strict-mineral-pattern + 5119 broader-other-bucket; the 1037 real-acreage figure and the 5416 non-spatial figure sum to 6453, which is 295 more than the 6158 total -- the strict-pattern and other buckets are not perfectly disjoint from the real-acreage bucket at their edges (a small number of rows have both a use code AND fall in the sampled-non-spatial description pattern). This card did not resolve that overlap to the row; it is sized approximately and flagged rather than force-reconciled to a clean partition.

whatContradictedTheCard: The dispatch names candidate CAD source columns to enumerate (geo_id, ref_id, situs, owner-account structures) 'do not guess' -- correctly cautious, but geo_id and ref_id do not exist in cad_property at all; the actual schema has no direct cross-reference column on either side. The real crosswalk key (situs_address + owner_name corroboration) had to be discovered empirically, not selected from an enumerated catalog, because the catalog does not contain a dedicated crosswalk field. Separately, the dispatch frames the Bastrop question as a single population needing one recommendation (companion vs out-of-fabric register); the data does not support a single answer -- the living>0 and $0 orphan populations sort into materially different mechanisms (72.6% parent-resolvable mobile homes vs 0% parent-resolvable non-spatial accounts), and the $0 population itself splits further into non-spatial accounts (majority) and a real geometry gap (minority, ~17%). A single recommendation would have been wrong for at least one of the three mechanisms found.

LESSON: When a dispatch names candidate schema columns for a crosswalk, verify with \d before querying -- the named columns (geo_id, ref_id) did not exist here, and trusting the dispatch's guess would have wasted the whole investigation.

A 1:1 uniqueness check on the join is mandatory before trusting any address-based crosswalk -- the raw exact-match join fanned out to 428,253 rows against only 282,569 R-prefix accounts, which would have silently produced a many-to-many mess if not caught immediately.

Free-text legal_description fields can carry a real, load-bearing parent-account reference (Bastrop's 'LOCATED ON R#####') that no structured column captures -- worth checking on any future orphan-account investigation before assuming no link exists. Also watch for source-data typos (LOCTED vs LOCATED) that a naive regex will silently miss.

An 'accounts without geometry' population that looks homogeneous in a summary count (8,712 / 6,158) can decompose into structurally different mechanisms once sampled -- do not design one solution for a population without first checking whether it IS one population.
GROUND-TRUTH: cad_property schema (all 21 columns) verified via \d, no geo_id/ref_id column exists
Williamson: 282,569 R-prefix / 319,480 numeric cad_property rows for county_fips=48491; 257,604 unique 1:1 situs matches; 92.2% owner-name corroboration
Bastrop: 8,712 living>0 / 6,158 $0 orphan accounts (county_fips=48021, not in txgio_parcel); 8,288 county-wide LOCA?TED-ON references, 99.2% resolve to a geometry-bearing parent
DEAD-END: A fixed numeric offset between R-prefix and numeric prop_ids (the early-roll sample R000009->62578, R000013->62579 looked sequential) -- does not hold across the full set and must not be used as a shortcut; the fan-out case (R022482, 64 candidates) has no single numeric counterpart at all.

Bastrop mechanism 1 (mobile homes): a follow-on card should design the companion representation shape on the parent feature and handle the 27.4% of living>0 orphans without a parent-link reference (characterize before assuming they're mechanism 2 or 3).

Bastrop mechanism 2 (non-spatial personal property, ~5,416 of 6,158 $0 orphans): needs a module-level not-applicable classification, separate from unaccounted, before an out-of-fabric register is built.
Bastrop mechanism 3 (1,037 real-acreage $0 orphans not in txgio_parcel): a genuine possible txgio geometry-fabric gap on rural/ag parcels, needs its own investigation, not solved here.
